newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sells crown, buys dollar - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sells crown, buys dollar - dealers.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Thursday sold Swedish crowns against the U.S. dollar, according to market traders.
The bank, which refused to comment on the rumoured intervention, was said to have moved when the crown reached 4.32 crowns to the mark and 6.64 to the dollar.
The move was said to have happened at around 0830 GMT.
"We don't comment on that," Riksbank dealer Anna Nordstrom told Reuters.
Four dealers told Reuters the move had happened.
This was the second time this week that the Riksbank was rumoured to have intervened in the market.
Traders said the central bank intervened on Monday after the crown began strengthened radpily in the wake of Finland linking the marrka to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
Again the bank refused to comment, adhering to its policy not to confirm or deny market talk.

Last month Riksbank spokesman Michael Wallin said the bank would increase buying and selling activity on the currency markets to stabilise the crown but this should not be seen in the context of possible preparation for ERM entry.
